To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(i) BNLC grammars define interesting graph languages, and (ii) the membership problem for these languages is solvable for a large class of graphs in deterministic polynomial time.
BNLC grammars generate a proper subclass of the NLC languages, but still enough generative and structural power remains to define a wide variety of graph languages of interest.
BNLC graph grammars are a useful tool for describing and analyzing graph languages and for proving the existence of graph languages with certain properties.
